who: William Gurnee Sinnigen, Roman historian at Hunter College/CUNY, PhD Michigan 1954.

evidence.says: Identifies William G. (William Gurnee) Sinnigen, author of The Officium of the Urban Prefecture; a 1965 citation identifies him as a Hunter College/CUNY history professor.

Marsh’s biography, pp. 47–48, records Michigan doctorate in 1954, Hunter appointment in 1962 and retirement in 1990, and explicitly names David A. Graves and Gershon Fogel Mamlak among his dissertation students.

notes: Doctorate, institution, dissertation subjects and both named students agree.

who: Warren F. Spencer, historian of diplomatic and naval history at the University of Georgia, PhD Pennsylvania 1955.

evidence.says: Warren F. Spencer is associated with Lynn M. Case’s The United States and France (1970).
Obituary records a history PhD from Penn in 1955, 21 years teaching at Georgia before retirement in 1988, and coauthorship with Lynn M. Case of The United States and France: Civil War Diplomacy.

notes: Same authored work connects the authority to the Georgia professor; doctorate and faculty period match.

who: Robert Poole Wilkins, historian at the University of North Dakota, PhD West Virginia 1954.

evidence.says: Identifies Robert Poole Wilkins as professor in the University of North Dakota history department, citing his papers for 1947–1980.
UND’s 1983 centennial history lists Robert P. Wilkins as an author affiliated with UND and identifies him in its catalogue metadata as Robert Poole Wilkins.
The scholarly article cites Robert P. Wilkins’s North Dakota and the European War, 1914–1917 as a West Virginia University PhD dissertation of 1954.

notes: Institution, field and doctorate match. The separate candidate n80070594 is a lawyer, not this historian.

who: John Maudgridge Snowden Allison, historian of France at Yale, PhD Princeton 1914.

evidence.says: Authorized name is John Maudgridge Snowden Allison.
Yale’s finding aid, p. 4, records Princeton PhD 1914 and Yale history appointments from 1914 through 1944, including European history professorships; identifies books on French history.

notes: Full name, Princeton doctorate and Yale appointment during both dissertation years agree.

who: Robert Anchor, modern European intellectual historian at the University of Southern California.

evidence.says: Identifies Robert Anchor, author of The Enlightenment Tradition (1967), as an assistant professor of history at the University of Southern California.
A publisher advertisement in the AHA’s 1977 program, p. 118, identifies Robert Anchor at USC as author of The Modern Western Experience, emphasizing modern Western cultural and intellectual history.

notes: Authority and contemporary publication identify the USC historian in the relevant period. Rochester doctorate was not independently verified.

who: John Francis Battick, history professor at the University of Maine, PhD Boston University 1967.

evidence.says: Identifies John F. Battick, PhD, as compiler of Vital Records of Dover-Foxcroft, Maine (2011).
Obituary records Boston University PhD in 1967, a University of Maine history appointment ending in retirement in 1997, and publication of Vital Records of Dover-Foxcroft.
University of Maine’s John Francis Battick collection identifies Professor John F. Battick and materials associated with his maritime history teaching, covering 1950–1997.

notes: The authority’s publication connects to the Maine professor; doctorate and field agree.

who: Jeremy Rossiter, classical archaeologist and history/classics faculty member at the University of Alberta since 1986.

evidence.says: Alberta’s 2020 curator profile identifies Jeremy Rossiter in History and Classics, joining its Faculty of Arts in 1986 and curating its ancient antiquities collection.
The candidate is Jenny Rossiter, author of Assets for Life and Nobler and Better Things; describes urban development and housing research, consultancy, and part-time teaching at UCL and Middlesex.

notes: The sole candidate has a different full name and a distinct career in housing and urban development; it is not Alberta’s classical scholar.

who: Philippe Genequand, medieval historian at Université de Montréal, PhD Université de Genève.

evidence.says: Identifies Philippe Genequand, author of Une politique pontificale en temps de crise (2013), as professor of medieval history at Université de Montréal.
Department profile records a Geneva PhD, lists the same 2013 book, and explicitly lists the doctoral theses of Louis Provost-Brien (2019) and Sébastien Filion (2018) under his supervision.

notes: Authority, institution, book and both named doctoral students agree.
